statement: `NONE` `100/100` `9df6a482767136f31519324c254be3f2dca5341bde7bdebf239c7dec5e746c29` `"endpoint scheme" graph-realizable 3-uniform hypergraph` A 3-uniform hypergraph \(H\) is isomorphic to \(\mathcal T(G)\) for some simple graph \(G\) if and only if there is an equivalence relation \(\sim\) on \(V(H)\times\{0,1\}\) such that: 1. \((e,0)\not\sim(e,1)\) for every \(e\in V(H)\); 2. distinct \(e,f\) do not determine the same unordered pair of equivalence classes; 3. for every \(\{e,f,g\}\in E(H)\), the three unordered endpoint pairs determined by \(e,f,g\) are exactly the edges of a triangle; 4. every triple of hypergraph vertices whose endpoint pairs form a triangle is a hyperedge of \(H\). Conditions (1)-(2) make the graph simple, while (3)-(4) say exactly that its graph triangles are the hyperedges of \(H\).

proof: The suppressed kernel has minimum degree at least three, no loops, and cyclomatic number three. Hence sum_v(deg(v)-2)=2|E|-2|V|=4, so it has at most four vertices. It has at least two because a loop would make the unsuppressed branch vertex a cut vertex. With two vertices, looplessness forces equal degrees and the excess equation gives four parallel edges. With three vertices, 2-connectivity makes every pair adjacent; the degree sequence is 4,3,3 and solving the three multiplicities gives 2,2,1. With four vertices every degree is three. If all multiplicities are at most one the graph is K4. Otherwise a parallel pair has multiplicity exactly two. Its endpoints each have one remaining edge, necessarily to distinct other vertices; the remaining two edges must be a parallel pair between those vertices. This is D22.

statement: Let a finite fiber-coherence CSP have a tree-absorbed 2-connected incidence block. Suppress each maximal degree-two path. Give every remaining branch node its surviving state domain. For every kernel edge e, let R_e be the binary relation of branch-state pairs extendable through its suppressed path. Then the original block has a coherent section if and only if the binary CSP on the branch kernel with edge relations R_e has a solution.
proof: A coherent section restricts to one state at every branch node and hence to a pair in R_e on every path. Conversely, choose branch states satisfying every R_e. Maximal degree-two paths have disjoint interiors; the exact path witnesses and all previously absorbed trees therefore extend independently and glue at the common branch states.

statement: For finite sets A,B and any relation R subset A x B, there is a finite K4-free stable-partition graph gadget with boundary fibers X indexed by A and Y indexed by B such that a boundary choice (a,b) extends to a coherent section of the gadget if and only if (a,b) belongs to R. The gadget has four realized triangle types arranged in a path.
proof: Use six stable parts A0,A1,P0,P1,B0,B1. Put boundary edges x_a=A0(a)A1(a) and y_b=B0(b)B1(b). For every (a,b) in R create private vertices p0(a,b),p1(a,b) and edges A1(a)p0, A0(a)p0, p0p1, A1(a)p1, p1B0(b), p0B0(b), p1B1(b). The quotient on the six parts is the square of a six-vertex path, so its clique number is three and the graph is K4-free. Its only triangles are the four consecutive triples, one chain for each allowed pair. The first triangle forces the A-label a onto the pair state (a,b), the middle two carry that state, and the last forces the B-label b. Thus the exact boundary projection is R.

statement: For every integer q at least 2, the binary CSP with q+1 variables, domain [q], and inequality on every pair of variables is inclusion-minimal incoherent. Its binary constraint graph is K_(q+1), with cycle rank q(q-1)/2.
proof: The full CSP asks for q+1 distinct colors from q colors and is impossible. After deleting one inequality constraint uv, assign u and v the same color and biject the remaining q-1 variables to the remaining q-1 colors. Hence every one-constraint deletion is coherent. The cycle-rank formula is |E(K_(q+1))|-|V(K_(q+1))|+1=q(q-1)/2.

statement: Every finite binary CSP has a polynomial-size realization as the exact boundary projection of a finite K4-free fiber-coherence system. One stable boundary fiber represents each CSP variable, and one private R3K03 strip represents each binary constraint.
proof: Create one stable pair of parts and one matching edge per domain value for every variable. For each binary constraint, attach a fresh R3K03 relation strip to the two corresponding boundary fibers. Different strips have disjoint private parts and no cross-strip edges. Therefore every triangle lies in one strip. A K4 meeting private vertices from two strips would need a cross-strip edge, while a K4 contained in one strip is excluded by R3K03. A global coherent section chooses one shared value edge for each variable and extends through each strip exactly when every binary relation is satisfied. The number of vertices and edges is linear in the explicitly listed relation tables.

statement: Given a finite K4-free graph together with its stable partition and realized triangle-type fiber system, deciding whether a coherent section exists is NP-complete. NP-hardness holds with branch domains of size three.
proof: A proposed section lists one representative edge per nonempty fiber and can be checked against all realized triangle types in polynomial time, so the problem is in NP. Reduce graph 3-COLORING: make one three-value variable per input vertex and one inequality relation per input edge, then apply R3K05. Coherent sections are exactly proper three-colorings, and the output graph is K4-free.

statement: For the four-parallel-edge kernel Q4 with branch domains S,T and path relations R1,R2,R3,R4 subset S x T, coherence is equivalent to R1 intersect R2 intersect R3 intersect R4 being nonempty.
proof: R3K02 reduces the block to one common state pair that must satisfy all four parallel edge relations. This is exactly membership in the four-way intersection.

statement: For the D22 kernel, intersect each doubled opposite edge pair to obtain relations P and Q. Orient the two remaining single relations S,T around the resulting four-cycle. The block is coherent if and only if the composition P o S o Q o T contains a fixed point.
proof: Parallel kernel edges impose both relations, hence their intersections. After this compression the branch-kernel CSP is one binary relation cycle. Apply the fixed-point criterion UC04.

statement: For the T221 kernel with branch nodes A,B,C, let P be the intersection of the two A-B relations, Q the intersection of the two A-C relations, and T the B-C relation. The block is coherent if and only if there exist a,b,c with P(a,b), Q(a,c), and T(b,c).
proof: R3K02 gives five binary edge constraints. The two parallel pairs are simultaneously satisfied exactly by P and Q. The remaining condition is the displayed three-relation join.

statement: For the simple K4 branch kernel with branch domains D1,D2,D3,D4 and six edge relations R_ij, coherence is equivalent to the existence of (x1,x2,x3,x4) in the domain product satisfying R_ij(xi,xj) for every pair i<j.
proof: This is R3K02 specialized to the six edges of the K4 kernel.

statement: Every finite tree-absorbed 2-connected fiber-coherence block of cycle rank three is exactly one of four relation mechanisms: 1. Q4 four-way intersection; 2. T221 ternary join after two parallel intersections; 3. D22 cycle monodromy after two parallel intersections; 4. a four-variable K4 binary CSP. There is no fifth branch-kernel mechanism at cycle rank three.
proof: R3K01 exhausts the possible branch kernels. R3K07 through R3K10 give the exact coherence test for each kernel.

statement: Finite fiber coherence on a tree-absorbed 2-connected incidence block of cycle rank at most three is decidable, with a section or exact failure certificate, in polynomial time in the explicit relation-table size.
proof: Ranks zero, one, and two are handled by CC12, UC05, and TH03. At rank three use R3K11. Q4 uses intersection, T221 uses a fixed-size join, D22 uses relation composition, and K4 enumerates at most the product of four branch-domain sizes, a polynomial of fixed degree.

statement: The K4-kernel CSP with four variables, domain {0,1,2}, and inequality on all six edges is inclusion-minimal incoherent. Every relation is fully supported, and every one-edge-deleted rank-two subblock is coherent.
proof: Four variables cannot be pairwise distinct in a three-element domain. After deleting edge uv, set u=v and assign the other two variables the remaining two colors in either order. Inequality projects onto every value at both ends, so all relations are fully supported.

statement: The intrinsic K4 inequality mechanism of R3K13 cannot be inclusion-minimal on a two-element domain, while a three-element domain suffices.
proof: With two colors, every K4-minus-edge graph still contains a triangle and is not two-colorable, so one-edge deletions do not all repair the core. R3K13 supplies the three-color construction.

statement: There is a finite K4-free stable-partition graph whose fiber-coherence projection is the intrinsic three-color K4 kernel of R3K13. It has no coherent section, while deleting any one complete relation-strip block restores coherence.
proof: Apply R3K05 to the six inequality relations of R3K13. Exact projection preserves solutions and block deletions, and R3K05 guarantees K4-freeness.

statement: For the six inequality blocks of the three-color K4 core: 1. deleting one block gives exactly 6 solutions; 2. deleting two adjacent K4 edges gives exactly 12 solutions; 3. deleting two disjoint K4 edges gives exactly 18 solutions.
proof: With one missing edge, its endpoints must share a color; choose that color in 3 ways and order the remaining colors in 2 ways. With two adjacent missing edges, exactly one of the two missing pairs is the repeated-color pair: choose which pair in 2 ways and then a bijection of three colors to the three color classes in 3!=6 ways. With two disjoint missing edges, either exactly one missing pair is equal (2*3! choices) or both are equal (3! choices), totaling 18.

statement: In the R3K13 core, the pair-deletion number D_ef equals 12 exactly when constraint edges e,f share a K4 endpoint, and equals 18 exactly when they are disjoint. Hence the second-order deletion profile reconstructs the line graph L(K4), and therefore the full adjacency geometry of the six constraint blocks.
proof: This is the geometric reading of R3K16. The 12 pairs with value 12 are exactly adjacent edge pairs, and the 3 pairs with value 18 are the three opposite-edge pairs. These relations are the octahedral line graph L(K4).

statement: Among the 3^4=81 assignments of the R3K13 core, the numbers violating j inequality constraints are N_0=0, N_1=36, N_2=18, N_3=24, N_6=3, and N_j=0 otherwise.
proof: Classify assignments by color multiplicities. Type 2+1+1 has one equal pair and count 3*C(4,2)*2=36. Type 2+2 has two equal pairs and count 3*3*2=18. Type 3+1 has three equal pairs and count 3*4*2=24. Type 4 has six equal pairs and count 3. These exhaust all assignments.

statement: For the q-color K_(q+1) core of R3K04: 1. every one-edge deletion has q! solutions; 2. two adjacent edge deletions have 2q! solutions; 3. two disjoint edge deletions have 3q! solutions; 4. N_1=binom(q+1,2)q! and N_2=3 binom(q+1,4)q!.
proof: The one- and two-deletion counts use the same color-class argument as R3K16. For N_1, sum the q! solutions over all one-edge deletions and use PG01. For N_2, sum all pair-deletion counts. There are (q+1)binom(q,2) adjacent edge pairs and 3binom(q+1,4) disjoint pairs. PG02 at r=2 gives sum D=(m-1)N_1+N_2, which simplifies to the stated formula.

statement: Let r be fixed and d bound every fiber domain. Finite fiber coherence on incidence graphs of cyclomatic number at most r is decidable in O(d^r poly(N)) time. In contrast, without a cycle-rank bound the problem is NP-complete even for K4-free graph realizations with domain size three.
proof: Choose a spanning forest. For each of at most r nonforest incidence edges, select its variable endpoint; deleting these at most r variable nodes leaves a forest. Apply the feedback-conditioning algorithm UC06. The unbounded-rank hardness is R3K06.

statement: For every stable finite-fiber compression of a hypothetical Erdős #595 witness, one of the following holds: 1. a finite incoherence core has incidence cycle rank at most three and is exactly certified by the forest, unicyclic, theta/cactus, or R3K11 algorithms; 2. a finite minimal core has cycle rank at least four; 3. every finite subsystem coheres and compactness gives a full coherent section, yielding an exact uncountably chromatic Berge-C3-free hypergraph compression.
proof: CC19 gives finite obstruction or exact compression. Choose a minimal finite core in the obstruction branch. The inherited forest/cactus/rank one/rank two results and R3K11 classify every core through rank three; otherwise its rank is at least four.

statement: `HG01` `100/100` `3bdd25f6f4e0a622983acecbf7aaedee971eeefd7aff9e9eefa722f8d3d0e6f7` `"quotient graph" bipartite cover triangle-cover partition` Let \(\mathcal P\) be a partition of \(V(G)\), and let \(Q_{\mathcal P}\) be the quotient graph whose vertices are the parts and whose edges are the pairs of parts joined by at least one edge of \(G\). statement: `NONE` `100/100` `c952a047602c9350e2d31c5765a992e85dfaf09b6d22fd6eacd3d5599c0efc6f` `"every graph" quotient of matching stable partition` Every simple graph \(Q\) is the quotient graph of a matching under a partition into stable sets. statement: `0d932677571443ad09574af611c80611fe06e8ecfee7497986531c66a72bf4ad` `"κ-complete ideal" triangle-free edge cover` Let \(\kappa\) be an infinite cardinal and \(G\) a graph. statement: `71823612fc62acb81d98b98ac699a1bc54be35f549387390a7fcc86aa1c1758d` `"triangle cover number" deletion persistence edge ideal` Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. statement: `60234c81b65413cf19871eecf39e36ca94daa6794e2b3f7fcec7985b8917c4c3` `"triangle cover" countable vertex deletion robustness` Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. statement: Let \(B\) be a finite simple 2-connected graph with cyclomatic number \[ |E(B)|-|V(B)|+1=2. \] Then exactly two vertices of \(B\) have degree three, every other vertex has degree two, and \(B\) is the union of three internally vertex-disjoint paths with the same two endpoints.
proof: Since \(B\) is 2-connected, every degree is at least two. Also \[ \sum_{v\in V(B)}(\deg v-2)=2|E|-2|V|=2. \] The only possibilities are two degree-three vertices, or one degree-four vertex. The latter is impossible: deleting that vertex leaves a graph of maximum degree two with four degree-one incidences; it cannot be connected, so the deleted vertex would be a cut vertex. Thus there are exactly two degree-three vertices \(s,t\). Starting along each of the three edges incident with \(s\), degree-two vertices force a unique continuation. A continuation cannot return to \(s\) without meeting \(t\), because that would make \(s\) a cut vertex. Hence the three continuations terminate at \(t\), are internally disjoint, and cover every edge by connectedness.
